title: Combinatorial Search for Strong Shift Equivalence
summary: The most important open problem of symbolic dynamics consists in finding a procedure to decide whether two subshifts of finite type are conjugate or, equivalently, whether two nonnegative integer matrices are strong shift equivalent. While the problem remains hard in general, the literature also contains specific examples of matrices that are not known to be strong shift equivalent: the Baker matrices, and Ashley's eight-by-eight.
